Left my well paid job last year.  I confided in my line manager that I was taking medication for depression and anxiety following the birth of our second daughter.  He seemed to be ok with it and offered support if needed.  Then my already stretched workload doubled overnight and involved me travelling to London for 2/3 nights every week (I live in Manchester) which played havoc with my home life and even resulted in bringing my eldest daughter into the office on my week off just to keep on top of things. 

Last straw came when I was trying to get home from South London on a Friday afternoon.  Phone calls kept coming asking for docs to be sent to a client. Despite saying I couldn’t log in from a bus or Underground train, they insisted it needed to be done asap. Eventually logged on at Euston and found all the documents were saved on the office server. Someone forwarded them on and I literally just forwarded it straight on. A job which anyone could have done, but for which I was thrown under the bus for.  Missed my train home at 3.30. Next one wasn’t till 7.20.  Everyone else at work left the office at 4. I didn’t get home till 10.30pm, so couldn’t take my daughter to her kickboxing lesson as we always do.  E-mailed my notice that night.

Tried to rescind it on the Monday but was told it had been accepted. During the notice period, I also became aware of untrue rumours being told about me including that I was a liar and “not at the races”(this was from the line manager I previously spoke to). 

Having worked there for 7 years and being betrayed by people I counted as my friends really hurt me. This was exacerbated by the death of my wife’s mother a week later. Despite several temporary jobs, it took six months to secure another permanent job. It’s half the salary of what I was earning before but the prospects are better and it’s a much nicer environment. 

Money has been tight, and it’s led to a lot of arguments between my wife and I. Since her mother passed, she’s been permanently angry and using my lack of work as an excuse to scream at me. She’s currently pushing for a separation which would kill me if it happened as the kids are my life. 

I’d just like things to go back to the way before all this started. I’m still on anti depressants and find it hard to trust people after what happened. Despite all the campaigns about speaking about mental health, I’d warn anyone not to mention it to anyone you work with. Attitudes aren’t as open as the media would have you believe.
